thread.title: The 2007 unsolved puzzling cases of two teens: Kelly Gaskins and Virginia Wood from North Carolina
thread.title_full: The 2007 unsolved puzzling cases of two teens: Kelly Gaskins and Virginia Wood from North Carolina

author: CJ Coombs
title: The 2007 unsolved puzzling cases of two teens: Kelly Gaskins and Virginia Wood from North Carolina
text:
5 hours ago Kelly Gray Gaskins. Photo by NCMEC website. As of today, 68 missing children in North Carolina, spanning from 1962 to 2026, were reported to and listed with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC).
Kelly Gray Gaskins , pictured above, has been missing from Dover, North Carolina (Beaufort County), since January 1, 2007, according to the NCMEC. According to The Charley Project, she's been missing since January 15, 2007, when she reportedly called her mother. Other sources indicate it was January 18, 2007, when her mother last heard from her.
Kelly's photo below is an age-progressed representation of how she might have looked at 34, though she would now be 38 if she's still alive.
Kelly Gray Gaskins' age-progressed photo. Photo by NCMEC website. About Multiple sources indicate that 19-year-old Kelly left for Brownsville, Texas with her boyfriend, Ervin Braxton "Gotti" Williams, the day after Christmas in 2006. Kelly was last believed to be in the area of Matamoros, Mexico, near the Texas border. Her nickname is "Kilo."
On January 9, 2012, the true-crime series, Disappeared , featured missing Virginia Lynne "Ginni" Wood and Kelly Gaskins in Season 5, Episode 1, titled "The Road Not Taken." (It's still available to watch on Amazon Prime.) I watched it twice.
In the episode, the mothers of Ginni and Kelly are interviewed as well as an investigator with the Beaufort County Sheriff's Department, and an attorney who went to Matamoros, Mexico to help find some answers. The disappearances of all three individuals lead to theories and speculation.
Physical description When Kelly went missing, she was between 5'3" and 5'4" tall and weighed between 90 and 100 pounds. Kelly has a tattoo of a sun in black ink with curvy rays and a peace symbol in the center on her right shoulder blade. There are more photos of Kelly on The Charley Project website. She was classified as an endangered missing person.
When Ginni went missing, she was 5'6" tall and weighed 190 pounds. She's been missing from Boone, North Carolina, since March 8, 2007, according to the NCMEC. She was also classified as an endangered missing person.
Ginni had brown hair that was dyed red and hazel eyes. She has a small reddish birthmark below her right eye and a two-inch scar on the inside of her left thigh. Her eyebrow is pierced, and she wears eyeglasses. She's been described as shy and a strong student.
According to the Community United Effort, also known as (CUE) Center for Missing Persons, at the time, Virginia was a Dean’s List student at Appalachian State University .
In March 2007, Ervin was 23 years old. He was described as Caucasian, 5'9" to 6'0" tall, and 170 pounds, with brown hair and blue eyes. His nickname is "Gotti."
Details Kelly and Ervin (pictured below) reportedly left Chocowinity, North Carolina, the day after Christmas in 2006, in a 1987 Mercury Cougar.
The last time Kelly's mother heard from her daughter was when she called her in January 2007. Some sources indicate the call was on January 15, 2007, from Texas. The Doe Network indicates the call was on January 18, 2007 , from Matamoros, Mexico. She and her boyfriend were believed to be in that area of the Texas border and working at a hotel.
According to Kelly's mother, it seemed like ever since her daughter began her relationship with Ervin in 2005, he became her priority. Her mother didn't approve of him, and the mother-daughter relationship changed after that. Kelly struggled in her senior year in high school, still failing when she repeated the 12th grade.
At the time, Ervin and Kelly were wanted by the police. Kelly was wanted for a probation violation. She was on misdemeanor probation for drug possession in North Carolina and violated parole by leaving the state. Ervin was reportedly planning to avoid prosecution of his more serious crimes by traveling to Mexico.
Ervin Braxton Williams would be 42 now. Photo by NCMEC website. At one point, Kelly moved in with Ginni and her family. She stayed for around six months. She returned home in the summer of 2006.
Ervin and his father were involved in a criminal activity involving arson, and after his father committed suicide on January 8, 2007, this left Ervin alone to answer for their crimes. According to the Disappearance documentary, Ervin's brother also committed suicide.
When Kelly called her mother on January 18, 2007, she told her mother that wherever she was in Mexico, it wasn't what she expected. In early March 2007, 19-year-old Ginni traveled to Texas to meet up with Kelly and Ervin during her spring break.
On March 10, 2007, Ginni called a friend from Texas to say that she and Kelly were going to go to Cancun. Virginia's black 2003 Nissan Sentra with North Carolina license plate number TTZ-6801 disappeared with her, and it hasn't been recovered. There's confusion when other sources indicate that the Nissan Sentra was Kelly's vehicle.
Virginia Lynne Wood would be 38 now. Photo by NCMEC website. Ervin is wanted for failure to appear in court to answer to charges of arson, burglary, cocaine and marijuana possession, and assault. He reportedly planned to go to Mexico to escape prosecution.
Law enforcement considered Kelly a fugitive for years and wouldn't accept a missing person's report for her, but one was finally filed in 2015. The families of Kelly and Ginni were concerned about their safety.
Kelly, Virginia, and Ervin were never heard from again (according to The Charley Project). There were rumors Ervin was back in Beaufort County with no sign of Kelly, but that was never confirmed and was believed to be untrue.
Kelly is listed in the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NamUs), case #MP4999 , an official website of the U.S. Department of Justice. NamUs indicates that Kelly's mother last heard from her on January 18, 2009, which would be two years after she went missing. The year may be an error.
Kelly is also listed under case #3588DFNC on The Doe Network, with a missing date as of January 18, 2007. Her dental, fingerprint, and DNA information are available for future identification.
If you have any information regarding Kelly’s disappearance, please reach out to the Beaufort County Sheriff's Office at 1-252-946-7111 and reference agency case no. 07L03605.
You can also contact the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) through its website at https://www.missingkids.org or its 24/7 call center at 1-800-843-5678, and reference NCMEC #1244697.
Thank you for your time to read and share.
